Barber Room 183, 1961 East Mall Vancouver V6T 1Z1 BC Canada JOB POSTING INFORMATION Placement Term <b> Job Title <b> Position Type Job Location Country Duration Work Mode Salary Currency Salary Job Description Job Summary 2026 - Summer S26 Co-Op Emerging Media Software Developer 178651 Co-op Position Vancouver, BC Canada 4 months In-Person CAD 22.0 per hour for 35 Major List UBC's Emerging Media Lab is an experimental space in which faculty, students and staff from all disciplines collaborate to evolve learning through the creation of educational tools using emerging media. EML projects have used a variety of technologies and media including virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), Generative AI, machine learning, brain-computer interfaces, etc. EML's objective is to create an incubation environment for new ideas and to help with the creation of proofs of concept using emerging media to enhance teaching and learning at UBC. This starts with a project proposal from a faculty member and ends with a team of student workers assigned to develop the project in collaboration with staff and faculty. EML Co-Op Emerging Media Software Developers collaborate with faculty, students, and staff to assist in development and implementation of 2D and/or 3D user interfaces and objects for media including VR, AR, and the web. Co-op Emerging Media Software Developers also have the opportunity to learn from established industry professionals, to contribute to open-source projects, and to build skills ranging from C++, C#, JavaScript, Python, Unreal, Unity, project management, software documentation, and user experience design. The Emerging Media Software Developer's responsibilities include creating, implementing, and maintaining a VR/AR experience or other software tool for use in education as well as coordinating student teams, with the support of staff, during the implementation of the project. Networking and Mentorship - The student will receive direct mentorship from EML's industry consultants - The student will build on existing collaborations with experts both at UBC and other institutions who are developing similar applications - The student will be listed on EML website and will play a role in publicly explaining and distributing the projects - The student will be exposed to innovative research into emerging technologies such as VR/AR, BCI, etc. through literature review and connecting with industry specialists - The student may be involved in, and credited as co-author on a manuscript for publication in teaching and learning journals Workplace Skills and Professional Development Co-Op students will gain experience: - With VR/AR application design and development; - By contributing to open-source projects and developing their portfolios; - By disseminating research results through live presentation, production of manuscripts for publication in Scholarship of Teaching and Learning journals, other publishing activity and at conferences; - With improved interpersonal, written, and oral communication skills; - With creating and editing professional project documentation; - In project management and developing their leadership skills as the team leads for their projects. Orientation and Training - The student will receive the necessary training in project management and communication software and protocols by industry professionals; - The student will be introduced to EML, their roles and responsibilities within the team and what project resources are available within the department and UBC; - The student will be assigned to project-based tasks in collaboration with the project teams, and continue to report on progress using project management software; - Additional required training on advanced software applications or programing languages will be identified and facilitated by the supervising team member; - EML also offers learning opportunities such as hands on workshops and demo sessions on new technologies as they emerge. Support, Feedback and Reflection - At the beginning of the work term, the student will create individual goals they wish to accomplish over the project work period. - While the student will be encouraged to work on aspects of the project independently, they will be supported by, and be in communication with, various members of the project team throughout the work term - The student will meet with the project team weekly to assess project progress and direction, and to identify potential obstacles - There will be regular one-on-one meetings with their supervisor, subject matter experts and individual team members responsible for building content - Two development plan meetings will be held between the student and the project lead, halfway through and at the end of the work term, to review the student's development and progress towards their goals - The student will maintain a working log of progress, including a record of new skills and accomplishments - At the end of the project work period, the student will provide a summary of their learning experience that indicates the most valuable aspects of their experience, their progress towards their goals, and provides options for improving future Co-Op student experience in the project - The student will receive additional support from UBC Studios and UBC IT teams Supervision The student will: • Be directly supervised by Lab Supervisor; • Be mentored in technical skills by EML staff and industry consultants. Complexity of Task • Some tasks will require advanced problem solving and troubleshooting skills; • The student will be expected to communicate effectively with all team members on the progress and anticipated completion of components of the project; Documentation of the process and technical details is a critical component of the job. • Job Requirements Job Requirements • Assist in the development of new open-source teaching tools using VR & AR tools including Unity, Unreal, 3D modelling tools such as Maya and Blender, photogrammetry, 360-degree videos, etc.; • Attend weekly meetings with the project team; • Contribute to technical documentation; • Present work to the project team and to the larger UBC community; • Plan and execute user testing and aApply results of user testing to improve projects; • Work collaboratively within the team; • Problem solve, debug, and troubleshoot the project as needed; • Assist with EML presentations, workshops, and events; • Other duties as required. Qualifications - Proficiency in Unreal, Unity and/or other real-time 3D software -Experience with 3D computer modelling software platforms; - Experience in web and mobile application user experience (UX) design and development is desirable; - Knowledge of agile development is desirable; - Ability to work independently and within a team environment to complete tasks and solve problems effectively; - Proficient in basic office software including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint; - Evidence of excellent communication and project management skills; - Interest in 3D graphics and visualization; - Desire to learn new and emerging technologies; - Experience in writing technical documentation in a professional setting. The ideal candidate is proficient in Unreal, Unity, C++, C#/.NET/Mono and is experienced with developing VR and AR applications, or JavaScript. However, we are most interested in candidates looking to develop these skills. We encourage candidates with programming skills in any language, experience with 3D software, game engines, middleware integration, APIs, etc. to apply.
